protocol.py: 4 biology problems (2 errors, 2 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 56 stocks
   line 51:  p20_multi.aspirate(1, batch1_source_wells[i])
   At line 51 the tip went into colony 2 (well A2 in slot 4), colony 3 (well A3 in slot 4),
   colony 4 (well A4 in slot 4), colony 5 (well A5 in slot 4) and 52 more while it still
   carried pcr mix (well A1 in slot 2), colony 1 (well A1 in slot 4), colony 2 (well A2 in
   slot 4), colony 3 (well A3 in slot 4) and 53 more from an earlier step (this line did it
   7 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 56 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6,
   A7, A8, B2 and 48 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, B2 and 48 more in slot 4.
   Also reached 56 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, B2 and 48 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 51 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [96c85877e03d]

   line 65:  p20_multi.aspirate(1, batch2_source_wells[i])
   At line 65 the tip went into colony 10 (well A10 in slot 4), colony 11 (well A11 in slot
   4), colony 12 (well A12 in slot 4), colony 13 (well B1 in slot 4) and 48 more while it
   still carried pcr mix (well A1 in slot 2), colony 9 (well A9 in slot 4), colony 10 (well
   A10 in slot 4), colony 11 (well A11 in slot 4) and 29 more from an earlier step (this

   drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 52 other wells: wells A10,
   A11, A12, B1, B2, B3, B4, B10 and 44 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A10, A11, A12, B1, B2, B3, B4, B10 and 44 more in slot 4.
   Also reached 52 other wells: wells A10, A11, A12, B1, B2, B3, B4, B10 and 44 more in slot
   3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 65 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [dac05cc3e5e6]

3. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 64 wells never mixed after colony 1, colony 13, the liquid from well
C1 in slot 4, the liquid from well D1 in slot 4 and 60 more went in (5% of the well)
   line 52:  p20_multi.dispense(1, batch1_dest_wells[i])
   At line 52 the robot added colony 1, colony 13, the liquid from well C1 in slot 4, the
   liquid from well D1 in slot 4 and 60 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 56
   more in slot 3, which already held pcr mix (this line did it 8 times). The addition was
   5% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way.
   Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is
   not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down
   before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 56 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 56 more in slot 3 after line 52:
   `mix_after=(5, 17 to 18)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 17 to 18, well)`, with the
   volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide

findings.explanation: At line 52 the robot added colony 1, colony 13, the liquid from well C1 in slot 4, the liquid from well D1 in slot 4 and 60 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 56 more in slot 3, which already held pcr mix (this line did it 8 times).
